To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IT delivery-business alignment and IT changebusiness alignment are more strongly associated with firm revenues than IT investment-business strategyalignment in an emerging economy context.

IT deliverybusiness priority alignment and IT changes-business change alignment are more strongly associated with the IT investment-firm performance relationship than IT investment-business strategyalignment.
IT delivery-business alignment and IT changebusiness alignment moderate the relationship between software and service investments and firm revenues in the context of emerging economy firms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between IT investment and firm performance and its association with IT-business alignment in the Indian context.
the effect of IT-business alignment on the relationship between IT investment and firm performance in emerging markets.
the relationship between IT-business alignment and IT investment and firm performance in an emerging market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alignment of IT investments to business priorities is the key factor that influences firm performance in emerging economies.
IT change-business change is a key driver for firms’ IT-business alignment and firm performance in emerging market contexts.
IT change-business change and IT delivery-business priorities alignment are important dimensions of alignment for IT investments to positively impact firm performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effect of IT investment on firm revenue is contingent upon the dimensions of IT business alignment, and that IT change-business change and IT delivery-business priorities are more strongly associated with firm performance.
IT investments are more effective in generating firm revenues when IT-business alignment is at the IT changebusiness change alignment dimension.
the alignment between IT investments and the business strategy is not sufficient to achieve the desired business outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between IT and business outcomes depends on the type of IT investments and alignment.
the relationship between IT investment and firm performance is moderated by the degree of alignment between IT and other business dimensions.
IT investments are associated with the dimensions and not the level of IT-business alignment.
